title: Fence Company Software: 6 Tools That Book More Jobs
html:
Fence company software starts with three tools. You need a job management app such as Jobber or Housecall Pro, an estimate and invoice app such as Joist, and a website. Start with a website and a free Google Business Profile. Add scheduling software once calls turn into jobs faster than you can track them. Published plans run from $10 to $299 a month.

Fence company software has to do three jobs: catch the lead, price the job and get paid. Most fence contractors buy tools in the wrong order and pay for features they never open. This guide sorts six tools by the job each one does, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Fence work is a quote-heavy trade. A homeowner asks three companies for a price, and the first clear estimate often wins. So this list starts with how a lead becomes a signed estimate. Then it covers the website and map listing that bring the lead in.

Which fence company software runs jobs and scheduling?

Jobber and Housecall Pro are the two job management apps most fence companies compare first. Both cover scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments in one place.

Both charge card processing fees on top of the plan price, and Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents. A fence company that closes a few large jobs a month feels those fees. Ask each vendor for the processing rate before you commit.

What fence contractor software handles estimates and invoices?

Joist is built for estimates, invoices and online payments, which makes it a light choice for a small fence crew that does not need dispatch.

  • Joist: sends estimates and invoices, takes online payments and tracks jobs. Basics is $10 a month billed monthly, and Pro is $17 a month billed monthly. Limit: Basics allows up to 5 documents a month, and the free plan is no longer offered.

Quote speed matters more than quote polish in this trade. A fence estimate needs linear feet, gate count, material and removal of the old fence. Whatever app you use, build a template for each fence type so a quote goes out the same day as the site visit.

Which website builders suit a fence company?

Wix and Squarespace both let a fence company launch a basic site without a developer. A builder only gives you the tool, not the leads. Check each vendor's plan page for your country, because prices depend on region.

  • Wix: a drag and drop builder with hosting and templates. Prices on its published plans are for yearly subscriptions paid in full, and a custom domain needs a paid plan. Limit: storage is 2 GB on the Light plan.
  • Squarespace: a template-based builder with invoicing and scheduling tools. Its Basic plan has 2 contributors and charges a 2% fee on online store sales. Limit: price display changes by country, so check the vendor for your figure.

A builder site still needs service pages for each fence type, a quote form and fast mobile loading. That is a managed build, not a do it yourself builder, so it costs more than Wix or Squarespace.

Which free tool puts a fence company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your fence company in Google Maps and local search. Google states that creating a profile is free.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, photos, reviews and phone number when homeowners search for a fence installer nearby. Limit: it needs regular photos, posts and review replies to stand out, and Google's paid products are separate.

Photos of finished fences and fast replies to reviews do most of the work here. If you are replying to reviews yourself, read how to handle a negative review first.

How do you choose fence company software?

Choose fence company software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Cost: add the plan price, extra users and card processing fees, then compare against one average fence job.

Setup effort: can one person set up templates and import customers in a weekend, or does it need training?

A small shop with one crew can run on Joist for quotes, a Wix or Squarespace site and a free Google Business Profile. A multi-crew company that schedules several installs a week fits Jobber or Housecall Pro better, with the website and map listing handled by a marketing partner.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Search ads from fence Google Ads and rankings from fence SEO send homeowners to the website, and Meta Ads for fence companies can reach homeowners before they search.

What software does a fence company need?

A fence company needs a way to quote jobs, schedule installs and take payment. It also needs a website and Google Business Profile so homeowners can find it. Start with estimates and invoices, then add scheduling software once you book several jobs a week.

How much does fence contractor software cost?

Published plans in this guide run from $10 a month for Joist Basics, billed monthly, to $299 a month for Housecall Pro MAX, billed annually. Card processing fees, extra users and add-ons cost more. Check the vendor's published prices before you decide.

Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a fence company?

Both handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so the better one depends on team size and add-ons. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually.

Do fence companies need a website if they use job software?

Yes. Job software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A website with a page for each fence type and a quote form gives homeowners a reason to call you instead of a competitor.

Is Google Business Profile free for a fence company?

Google states that creating a Business Profile and showing your business on Google is free. It still takes work: photos of finished fences, accurate service areas and replies to every review. Google's paid ad products are separate.

What should a small fence crew buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a simple website first. Then add an estimate and invoice app such as Joist. Move to full job management only when scheduling several crews becomes the bottleneck.
